title: Pickles and the stolen World Cup
hook: In 1966 the World Cup trophy went missing, and a dog out for a walk found it.
peek: A week after the World Cup trophy was stolen from a London exhibition in 1966, a collie called Pickles found it wrapped in newspaper under a garden hedge. He became a national celebrity just as England went on to win the tournament.
lede: In March 1966, four months before England hosted the World Cup, the gold Jules Rimet trophy was stolen from a stamp exhibition at Central Hall in Westminster. Police searched for a week with no luck. Then, on 27 March, a black and white collie named Pickles, out walking with his owner David Corbett in south London, stopped to nose at a parcel under a hedge.

bullets.text: Corbett unwrapped the newspaper and found a gold figure of a winged woman holding a cup, with the names of past winners on its base. He took it straight to the local police station.

bullets.opening: A reward and a film role
bullets.text: Corbett received a reward reported at about 6,000 pounds. Pickles became a star, appearing on television and in a 1966 comedy film, The Spy with a Cold Nose.

While the original was missing, the Football Association quietly had a copy made by a silversmith. The replica stood in for the real trophy at some public events and was later sold at auction, where FIFA bought it.
Brazil kept the Jules Rimet trophy for good after winning a third title in 1970. It was stolen again in Rio de Janeiro in 1983 and has never been found, so the one Pickles rescued is lost after all.
